title: Talking about past experiences / Gbakọta n'okpuru ụzọ gara aga
bridge: Na Igbo, tụọnụ okpuru ụzọ gara aga anyị na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'present perfect' ('emeela') ma ọ bụ 'past simple' ('emeela'), tụọnụ na ndị a na-akpọ 'present perfect' ('emeela') bụ na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' ('emeela'). Na English, tụọnụ okpuru ụzọ gara aga anyị na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'present perfect' ('have visited'), nke adịghị n'okpuru ụzọ doro anya na Spanish. Nke a bụ na ndị a na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'have + participle' na ndị a na-akpọ 'present perfect' na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' na ndị a na-akpọ 'present perfect' na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple'. Oge ọma: na English, ọ dịghị iji 'present perfect' na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple'.
rule: Iji gbakọta n'okpuru ụzọ gara aga na English, anyị na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'present perfect' na ndị a na-akpọ 'structure': have/has + participle. O nwere ike ịbanye na: 1) okpuru ụzọ gara aga ndị a na-akpọ 'experience' ndị a na-akpọ 'unspecified time' (I have visited Paris), 2) okpuru ụzọ gara aga ndị a na-akpọ 'past actions' na ndị a na-akpọ 'relevance to present' (She has lost her keys), 3) na ndị a na-akpọ 'adverbs' dị ka 'ever', 'never', 'already', 'yet', 'just', 'before'. Nke a na-akpọ 'negative' na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'have not' (haven't) ma ọ bụ 'has not' (hasn't). Nke a na-akpọ 'interrogative' na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'auxiliary' (Have you ever...?). Iji ajụ maka okpuru ụzọ gara aga, anyị na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'Have you ever + participle?' ma tụọ ndị a na-akpọ 'Yes, I have' ma ọ bụ 'No, I never have'. ọ dịghị iji 'present perfect' na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' (yesterday, last week, in 2010). Na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' (visited, went). Na A2, ọ dị mma ịnweta ndị a na-akpọ 'participles' na ndị a na-akpọ 'verbs' ndị a na-akpọ 'common' (go-gone, eat-eaten, see-seen, have-had).

concept_examples.text: Have you ever seen that movie?
concept_examples.translation: Ihe mere ị na-emeela anya ụlọ akụkọ a?

concept_examples.text: We have already finished our homework.
concept_examples.translation: Anyị emeela tụọnụ ndị a na-akpọ 'homework'.

common_error.explanation: Ahuụrụ m ụzọ gara aga anyị na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'present perfect' na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' (yesterday). tụọnụ na ndị a na-akpọ 'past simple' (visited). tụọnụ na ndị a na-akpọ 'present perfect' na ndị a na-akpọ 'unspecified time' (have visited). Nke a bụ na ndị a na-akpọ 'present perfect' + ndị a na-akpọ 'specific time' = ọma.

levels.label: Present Perfect with 'ever' and 'never'
levels.translation: Present Perfect na ndị a na-akpọ 'ever' na ndị a na-akpọ 'never'

examples.original: Have you ever been to London?
examples.translation: Ihe mere ị na-emeela anya ụlọ akụkọ a?
examples.note: Usamos 'ever' en preguntas para preguntar sobre experiencias en cualquier momento de la vida.

examples.original: I have never tried Thai food.
examples.translation: Nunca he probado comida tailandesa.
examples.note: Anyị na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'ever' na ndị a na-akpọ 'questions' tụọnụ na ndị a na-akpọ 'experiences' na ndị a na-akpọ 'any time' na ndị a na-akpọ 'life'.

examples.original: She has never flown in a plane.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi hæz ˈnɛvər floʊn ɪn ə pleɪn/
examples.translation: Adịghị m emeela ihe ọma Thai.
examples.note: Recuerda que 'flown' es el participio de 'fly', verbo irregular.

levels.label: Present Perfect with 'already' and 'yet'
levels.translation: Present Perfect na ndị a na-akpọ 'already' na ndị a na-akpọ 'yet'

examples.original: I have already eaten breakfast.
examples.translation: Emeela m tụọnụ ndị a na-akpọ 'breakfast'.
examples.note: 'Already' se usa en afirmaciones y significa 'ya' (más pronto de lo esperado).

examples.original: Have you bought the tickets yet?
examples.translation: ¿Ya has comprado los boletos?
examples.note: 'Already' na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'affirmations' ma na-akpọ 'already' na ndị a na-akpọ 'earlier than expected'.

examples.original: We haven't finished our project yet.
examples.translation: Ihe mere ị na-emeela tụọnụ ndị a na-akpọ 'tickets'?
examples.note: En negación, 'yet' se coloca al final y significa que algo no ha ocurrido hasta ahora.

examples.original: I have been to Peru.
examples.translation: Ahuụrụ m Peru (na ndị a na-akpọ 'unspecified time' na ndị a na-akpọ 'life').
examples.note: El 'present perfect' se usa sin tiempo específico, para experiencias.

examples.original: I went to Peru in 2019.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɛnt tə pəˈruː ɪn tuː ˈθaʊzənd nɪnˈtiːn/
examples.translation: Fui a Perú en 2019.
examples.note: 'Present perfect' na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'experiences' na ndị a na-akpọ 'unspecified time'.

examples.original: She has lived in Madrid for two years.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi hæz lɪvd ɪn məˈdrɪd fɔːr tuː jɪrz/
examples.translation: Mụrụ m n'ụlọ akụkọ a na 2019.
examples.note: El 'present perfect' se usa con 'for' + duración para hablar de acciones que continúan en el presente.

examples.original: He saw his friend yesterday.
examples.translation: Él vio a su amigo ayer.
examples.note: 'Past simple' na-eme ka ndị a na-akpọ 'past actions' na ndị a na-akpọ 'specific time expression' dị ka 'in 2019'.

title: Making Plans and Arrangements / Ime n'ulo na ndoro ndoro
bridge: Na Spanish, anyị na-eme ihe mere nke a na-akwado ndoro ndoro (present continuous) ma ọ bụ nke ga-emepụta (be going to + infinitive) iji kwuo n'ulo. Na Igbo, anyị na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị ka 'eme' ma ọ bụ 'na-eme' n'ime ụbọchị ndoro. N'ihi na na Igbo, anyị na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị ka 'eme' ma ọ bụ 'na-eme' n'ime ụbọchị ndoro. N'ihi na na Igbo, anyị na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị ka 'eme' ma ọ bụ 'na-eme' n'ime ụbọchị ndoro.
rule:
Iji mepụta ndoro ndoro na Igbo na A2, biko jiri ndekọ ndị a:

1. **Present continuous** (am/is/are + -ing): n'ime ndoro ndoro dị ugbu a na-akwado, na ụbọchị ma ọ bụ ebe. Ej. 'I'm seeing the doctor at 3.' (Meme n'ulo).

2. **Be going to** (am/is/are going to + infinitive): n'ime ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ihe mere nke adịghị iche. Ej. 'We're going to visit our grandparents.' (Anyị na-eme ihe mere).

3. **Will** (will + base verb): n'ime ndoro ndoro mere n'oge mere, ọkpụkpere ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro. Ej. 'I'll help you with that.' (Mere n'oge mere).

4. **Would like to** (would like to + infinitive): n'ime ndoro ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro ndoro. Ej. 'Would you like to come to my party?'

Cheta na na Igbo, anyị adịghị eme ka present simple mere ndoro ndoro (n'ihi na na Spanish, ọ bụrụ na ọ dị iche iche n'ime ndoro ndoro). Jiri 'be going to' ma ọ bụ 'present continuous' n'ime ndoro ndoro.

concept_examples.text: I'm meeting my friend at the cinema tonight.
concept_examples.translation: A ga-eme m n'ulo n'ụlọ ọrịa ndị a ga-abịa ugbu a.
concept_examples.phonetic: aɪm ˈmiːtɪŋ maɪ frend æt ðə ˈsɪnəmə təˈnaɪt

concept_examples.text: We're going to travel to Spain next summer.
concept_examples.translation: Anyị ga-emepụta ije nke Spain n'oge ndoro ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: wɪər ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ˈtrævəl tə speɪn nekst ˈsʌmər

concept_examples.text: I'll help you with your homework after class.
concept_examples.translation: A ga-enye gị aka n'akwụkwọ ndị a ga-abịa n'oge ndoro ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: aɪl help juː wɪð jɔːr ˈhəʊmwɜːrk ˈɑːftər klɑːs

concept_examples.text: Would you like to come to my birthday party?
concept_examples.translation: Ị ga-enwere ike ịbanye n'ime ụlọ igwe m n'oge ndoro ndoro?
concept_examples.phonetic: wʊd juː laɪk tə kʌm tə maɪ ˈbɜːrθdeɪ ˈpɑːrti

common_error.wrong: I meet my friend at the cinema tonight.
common_error.correct: I'm meeting my friend at the cinema tonight.
common_error.correct_alt: I'm going to meet my friend at the cinema tonight.
common_error.explanation: Ọ bụrụ na ndoro ndoro a na-akwado n'oge mere, na Igbo, anyị na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị ka 'eme' ma ọ bụ 'na-eme' n'ime ụbọchị ndoro. Na Igbo, anyị na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị ka 'eme' ma ọ bụ 'na-eme' n'ime ụbọchị ndoro. Na Igbo, anyị na-eme ka ndoro ndoro dị ka 'eme' ma ọ bụ 'na-eme' n'ime ụbọchị ndoro.

levels.label: Expressing Future Plans with 'going to'
levels.translation: Ime ndoro ndoro nke ga-emepụta n'ime 'going to'

examples.original: I'm going to visit my grandma this weekend.
examples.phonetic: aɪm ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ˈvɪzɪt maɪ ˈɡrændmɑː ðɪs wiːkˈend
examples.translation: A ga-emepụta m n'ulo n'ogo m n'izu ugbu a.
examples.note: Anyị na-eme ka 'be going to' + infinitive mere ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ndoro. Na Igbo, ọ na-akwado ka 'ga-eme'.

examples.original: She's going to start a new job in June.
examples.phonetic: ʃiːz ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə stɑːrt ə njuː dʒɒb ɪn dʒuːn
examples.translation: Ọ ga-emepụta ịbanye n'ime ọrụ ọhụrụ n'ime Juun.
examples.note: Cheta na 'going to' adịghị ebe ụfọdụ, ọ bụrụ na 'be' (is, am, are) na-eme.

levels.label: Making Fixed Arrangements with Present Continuous
levels.translation: Ime ndoro ndoro dị ugbu a n'ime present continuous

examples.original: I'm seeing the dentist at 4:30 tomorrow.
examples.phonetic: aɪm ˈsiːɪŋ ðə ˈdentɪst æt fɔː θɜːrti təˈmɒroʊ
examples.translation: A ga-abịa n'ụlọ ọrịa m n'izu anọ na otu ugbu a.
examples.note: Present continuous na-akwado na ndoro ndoro dị ugbu a. Na Igbo, anyị na-eme ka 'a ga-abịa' ma ọ bụ 'eme n'ụlọ'.

examples.original: We're having dinner with the Smiths on Friday.
examples.phonetic: wɪər ˈhævɪŋ ˈdɪnər wɪð ðə smɪθs ɒn ˈfraɪdeɪ
examples.translation: Anyị ga-eme nri n'ime ndoro ndoro n'izu Eke.
examples.note: N'ime ndoro ndoro dị ugbu a na-akwado, present continuous na-akwado n'ime Igbo.

levels.label: Inviting and Responding to Suggestions
levels.translation: Ime ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ nkwenye nkwenye

examples.original: Would you like to join us for lunch?
examples.phonetic: wʊd juː laɪk tə dʒɔɪn ʌs fɔːr lʌntʃ
examples.translation: Ị ga-enwere ike ịbanye n'ime nri anyị?
examples.note: Anyị na-eme ka 'would like to' mere ndoro ndoro ndoro. Na Igbo, ọ na-akwado ka 'ị ga-enwere ike'.

examples.original: Sure, I'd love to. What time?
examples.phonetic: ʃʊr aɪd lʌv tə wɒt taɪm
examples.translation: Ee, m ga-enwere ike. Kedu n'ime ụbọchị ole?
examples.note: Nkwenye ndoro ndoro dị ugbu a. 'I'd love to' na-akwado 'I would love to'.

examples.original: Sorry, I can't. I have another appointment.
examples.phonetic: ˈsɒri aɪ kænt aɪ hæv əˈnʌðər əˈpɔɪntmənt
examples.translation: Ụfọdụ, m adịghị enwe ike. Meme m n'ulo ọzọ.
examples.note: Iji kwuo ike n'oge mere, mee ka ọ dị mma. Jiri 'can't' ma ọ bụ 'cannot' n'oge mere.

title: Giving advice and recommendations / Nye ndoro na nkowa
bridge: Na Spanish, anyị na-eme ka ndoro dị ka subjunctive (I recommend that you go, you should go). Na English, subjunctive adịghị enyere na 'recommend' ma 'suggest' n'okpuru; anyị na-eme ka verb base ma obi + infinitive: 'I recommend you go', 'I suggest you try'. Anyị nwere 'should' (ga-eme ka) nke na-eme ka okwu dịrị mma karịa 'must'. Mmeghe ndoro adịghị ịmalite na subjunctive na Spanish: 'I recommend that you go' adịghị mma, mana 'I recommend you to go' adịghị mma n'okpuru 'recommend' nwere infinitive n'okpuru 'to' mgbe obi dị.
rule:
Ime ndoro na nkowa na English na level A2, biko jiri ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro:
1. **Should / Shouldn't + verb base**: n'eme ndoro ndoro. E.g: 'You should eat more vegetables.' 'You shouldn't stay up late.' (nke na-eme ka okwu adịghị). Enwereghị conjugation (he should, not he shoulds).
2. **You could + verb base**: n'eme nkowa ndoro ndoro. E.g: 'You could try yoga.'
3. **I recommend / I suggest + that + subject + verb base** (n'okpuru 'to' ma subjunctive n'okpuru 'that'). E.g: 'I recommend that you see a doctor.' Anyị nwereghị iji gerund: 'I recommend seeing a doctor.' ma 'I suggest trying this.'
4. **How about + gerund (-ing)?**: n'eme nkowa ndoro ndoro. E.g: 'How about going for a walk?'
5. **Why don't you + verb base?**: n'eme nkowa n'okpuru okwu ndoro. E.g: 'Why don't you take a break?'
Ndebe: Jiri 'must' n'eme ndoro, o bu ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro; 'must' bu ndoro ndoro. N'eme nkowa ndoro ndoro ndoro 'could' ma 'might'. Jiri n'okpuru 'recommend' ma 'suggest', adịghị enyere 'to' n'okpuru object: 'I recommend you to go' adịghị mma.

concept_examples.translation: I ga-eme ka i nwụrụ anụ mma.

concept_examples.text: I recommend that you talk to the teacher.
concept_examples.translation: A na-eme ka i kwuo ugbu a na nduzi.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˌrekəˈmend ðæt juː tɔːk tə ðə ˈtiːtʃər/

concept_examples.translation: Kedu ka ị ga-eme ka anyị nwere nkowa?

common_error.wrong: I recommend you to go to the doctor.
common_error.correct: I recommend that you go to the doctor.
common_error.correct_alt: I recommend going to the doctor.
common_error.explanation: Na Spanish anyị na-eme 'te recomiendo que vayas' ma 'te recomiendo ir', mana na English, n'okpuru 'recommend' adịghị enyere infinitive n'okpuru 'to' n'ime object. Ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'recommend + that + subject + verb base' ma 'recommend + gerund'. Mmeghe ndoro adịghị ịmalite na translation 'te recomiendo a ti ir' (na-eme ka 'recommend you to go'). Iji were mmeghe ndoro, jiri: 'recommend' na-akwado 'that' ma '-ing', adịghị 'to'.

examples.original: You should sleep more.
examples.translation: I ga-eme ka ị tụọ anụ mma.
examples.note: Jiri 'should' + verb base. Na Spanish, 'deberías' + infinitive.

examples.original: He shouldn't eat so much sugar.
examples.translation: Ọ nwereghị ịrị anụ mma ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Nke na-eme ka okwu adịghị 'shouldn't' + verb base. Enwereghị conjugation n'ime third person.

examples.original: We should study for the test.
examples.translation: Anyị ga-eme ka anyị nwere nkowa n'okpuru ndoro.
examples.note: 'Should' adịghị enweghị conjugation n'ime person: I should, you should, we should.

levels.label: Suggestions with could and how about
levels.translation: Nkowa ndoro ndoro ndoro could ma how about

examples.original: You could try the new restaurant.
examples.translation: I nwereghị ịma nkowa n'okpuru restaurant ọhụrụ.
examples.note: 'Could' na-eme ka nkowa ndoro ndoro, o bu ndoro ndoro karịa 'should'.

examples.original: How about going to the park?
examples.translation: Kedu ka anyị ga-eme ka anyị tụọ park?
examples.note: N'okpuru 'How about' jiri gerund (-ing).

examples.original: Could we leave early?
examples.translation: Anyị nwereghị ịma nkowa n'okpuru okwu ndoro?
examples.note: Anyị nwereghị ịma nkowa n'okpuru 'could' n'okpuru okwu ndoro.

levels.label: Formal recommendations with recommend and suggest
levels.translation: Ndoro ndoro ndoro recommend ma suggest

examples.original: I suggest that you take a break.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ səˈdʒest ðæt juː teɪk ə breɪk/
examples.translation: A na-eme ka ị tụọ ugbu a.
examples.note: Jiri 'that + subject + verb base' (n'okpuru 'to' ma subjunctive n'okpuru 'that').

examples.original: They recommend staying at the hotel.
examples.translation: Anyị na-eme ka anyị tụọ hotel.
examples.note: N'okpuru gerund mgbe obi adịghị n'ime subject.

examples.original: The teacher suggested that we practice every day.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈtiːtʃər səˈdʒestɪd ðæt wiː ˈpræktɪs ˈɛvri deɪ/
examples.translation: Nduzi na-eme ka anyị nwere nkowa ndoro ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: N'okpuru 'that' + verb base (adịghị 'practiced'). Nke a bu ndoro ndoro.
